memory_update.text: Consumer theme should be researched as a set of second-order infrastructure and supplier lanes, not as a simple retailer/brand screen.

Retail supplier networks and EDI/order-management plumbing are a high-priority underfollowed node because retailer-specific integrations and trading-partner maps can create operational switching costs.
Natural colors and clean-label reformulation inputs are a high-priority consumer-staples supplier node tied to regulatory and brand reformulation pressure.

Travel back-office infrastructure should be screened separately from OTAs and hotels because distribution, channel management, revenue management, payments, and fraud tools may capture travel complexity with different risk exposure.
Housing repair-and-remodel suppliers and specialty distributors may be better second-order consumer beneficiaries than homebuilders when affordability pressure reduces housing turnover.
Later layers need public-company universe construction, analyst-coverage checks, filing-based customer verification, and market-pricing checks before any candidate ranking.

summary: Consumer is too broad to research as one sector. Layer 1A decomposes it into six chokepoint-style lanes where demand is visible but public-market exposure may sit one or two steps away from obvious retailers, brands, hotels, homebuilders, or marketplaces. The highest-quality discovery lanes are: retail supply-chain networks and compliance plumbing; natural colors and clean-label reformulation inputs; travel distribution and back-office infrastructure; housing repair, remodel, and building-products suppliers; private-label and value-channel enablers; and consumer-finance / payments / fraud infrastructure. The intent is not to pick stocks yet, but to create a research map for obscure suppliers, low-coverage small/mid caps, and hidden customer-supplier dependencies.

supply_chain_nodes.bottleneck_hypothesis: The bottleneck is not generic software; it is embedded trading-partner maps, retailer-specific integrations, compliance workflows, and supplier adoption. If a network already connects major retailers and suppliers, switching costs may be operationally high even when customer budgets slow.
supply_chain_nodes.market_cap_hunting_notes: Prefer $300M-$10B market caps with high recurring revenue, net retention disclosure, customer count, transaction volume, or trading-partner count. Exclude companies whose retail exposure is too diluted or whose churn shows the network is replaceable.
supply_chain_nodes.node: Retail supplier networks, EDI, order-management, catalog, compliance, and replenishment plumbing
supply_chain_nodes.public_asset_hunting_notes: Search for small/mid-cap SaaS or network businesses with high recurring revenue, many retail/supplier connections, EDI roots, low glamour, and exposure to Walmart, Amazon, Target, Costco, grocers, off-price, or branded suppliers. Look for growth deceleration caused by macro/tariffs that may obscure durable network value.

supply_chain_nodes.why_it_matters: Ecommerce and discretionary purchases increasingly depend on acceptance rates, fraud control, chargeback economics, loyalty engagement, and consumer-credit availability. demand_drivers: Value-seeking consumers shifting spend toward discount, private-label, club, off-price, and marketplace channels.
Retailers and brands needing tariff, inventory, supplier-compliance, EDI, order-management, and replenishment systems as supply chains become more volatile.
Food, beverage, personal-care, and packaged-goods companies reformulating products around natural colors, clean labels, sugar reduction, functional ingredients, and regulatory pressure.
Travel demand shifting from post-pandemic revenge travel to more normalized but still infrastructure-heavy demand across hotels, online travel, airline services, cruise, and local experiences.
Housing affordability pressure extending repair-and-remodel cycles and favoring maintenance, rental, replacement, and trade-down beneficiaries rather than only new-home demand.
Consumer credit stress, fraud, chargebacks, loyalty economics, and alternative payment rails becoming second-order bottlenecks for ecommerce and discretionary spending.

theme_map.public_market_search_strategy: Run a two-lane funnel. First map reference leaders such as large retailers, ecommerce platforms, OTAs, hotel groups, home-improvement retailers, packaged-food companies, and payment networks only to identify demand signals. Then deliberately step down the chain into small/mid-cap public companies that provide software plumbing, ingredients, co-manufacturing, specialty distribution, housing inputs, loyalty/payment rails, fraud tools, testing/inspection, or compliance services. Prioritize companies where the consumer exposure is hidden in a narrow segment, where analyst coverage is low, where customer concentration can be verified, or where the asset is misclassified under industrials, software, ingredients, chemicals, distribution, or business services rather than consumer.
supply_side_constraints: Retailer-specific integrations, compliance logic, supplier onboarding, catalog accuracy, EDI maps, and order-management workflows can be difficult to replace once embedded.
Natural ingredient conversion can require qualification, stability testing, color consistency, raw-material sourcing, application know-how, and customer reformulation cycles.
Travel distribution depends on fragmented inventory, channel managers, GDS/OTA connectivity, revenue-management tools, payments, and fraud handling.

Housing repair and remodel suppliers face installer availability, distribution access, SKU complexity, freight cost, building-code requirements, and exposure to lumber, resin, metals, chemicals, or HVAC components.
Private-label growth requires co-manufacturing capacity, packaging, food safety certification, retailer audits, and national logistics scale.
Consumer-finance and ecommerce infrastructure is constrained by underwriting data, bank partnerships, fraud models, compliance, take-rate pressure, and merchant integration depth.
